speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your infant's condition, could you describe the specific activities or situations that seem to trigger these episodes of stridor and wheezing?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do the symptoms improve when the infant's neck is extended or when he is lying on his stomach? I also need to know if there is any history of recurrent respiratory infections or cyanotic spells during these episodes.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you observe any cyanosis or signs of respiratory distress during these episodes, and has the infant experienced any recent respiratory infections? REQUEST TEST: Laryngoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the laryngoscopy is normal, I suspect the issue originates below the vocal cords, possibly in the trachea or mainstem bronchi. REQUEST TEST: CT scan of the neck and chest with sagittal reconstruction to evaluate for vascular rings or tracheal compression.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest X-ray: Evidence of tracheal compression and a vascular ring suggestive of a double aortic arch; Barium Swallow: Compression of the esophagus and trachea consistent with a vascular ring; Echocardiogram: Confirmatory findings of a double aortic arch

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging confirms a double aortic arch causing tracheal and esophageal compression, which explains the positional stridor and feeding difficulties. DIAGNOSIS READY: Double Aortic Arch
